questionText:
A meld operation on two instances of a data structure combines them into one single instance of the same data structure. Consider the following data structures:

P: Unsorted doubly linked list with pointers to the head node and tail node of the list.

Q: Min-heap implemented using an array.

R: Binary Search Tree.

Which ONE of the following options gives the worst-case time complexities for meld operation on instances of size $n$ of these data structures?
explanation:
Step-by-step Explanation:

1. Unsorted Doubly Linked List (P):
• To meld two doubly linked lists given their head and tail pointers, set the `next` pointer of the tail of the first list to the head of the second list, and update the tail pointer.
• This requires a constant number of pointer manipulations, taking $\Theta(1)$ time.

2. Min-heap Implemented using an Array (Q):
• Concatenating two min-heap arrays of size $n$ yields an array of size $2n$.
• Applying Floyd's `buildHeap` algorithm to create a valid min-heap from this array takes linear time in the total number of elements, i.e., $\Theta(2n) = \Theta(n)$ time.

3. Binary Search Tree (R):
• Perform an in-order traversal of both BSTs to obtain two sorted arrays in $\Theta(n)$ time.
• Merge the two sorted arrays into a single sorted array of size $2n$ in $\Theta(n)$ time.
• Construct a balanced BST from the sorted array in $\Theta(n)$ time.
• Total time complexity = $\Theta(n) + \Theta(n) + \Theta(n) = \Theta(n)$.

Therefore, the correct worst-case time complexities are P: $\Theta(1)$, Q: $\Theta(n)$, R: $\Theta(n)$, which corresponds to Option (A).
